subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing - FinLytics follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing - FinLytics follow-up

Hi Samir — great conversation today, thanks for walking through your inference use case. Quick recap + next steps from my side.

Recap
- Workload: customer support summarization + reranking (mixed chat + batch), ~300M tokens/month today, forecast 600M-1.2B tokens/month in 2027 Q2 depending on rollouts.
- SLA & latency: target P95 latency <= 400ms for short-form summaries; sustained throughput target ~150k tokens/sec across the pool during peak windows.
- Security: will need SOC2 evidence and support for customer-managed VPC (we covered Private option briefly).

Pricing & capacity options (rough, ballpark ranges — see attached inference_estimate.xlsx):
- Option A — 8x A100 80GB reserved pool
  - Throughput (estimate): ~120k tokens/sec sustained (depends on batching + model).
  - Reserved sizing: 8 GPUs (dedicated)
  - Estimated committed price: $65k - $95k / month (varies with term & model)
  - Unit economics: ~ $700 - $1,100 per 1M tokens (based on forecasted monthly token volumes)

- Option B — 4x H100 reserved pool
  - Throughput: ~90k tokens/sec sustained
  - Estimated committed price: $40k - $60k / month
  - Unit economics: ~ $950 - $1,400 per 1M tokens

- Option C — 16x A100 (higher throughput, higher commit)
  - Throughput: ~220k tokens/sec
  - Estimated committed price: $120k - $165k / month
  - Unit economics: ~ $450 - $800 per 1M tokens (best scale efficiency)

Important notes:
- Unit economics are highly sensitive to: model family (decoder-only vs chat-optimized), quantization level, prefix caching effectiveness, and % of tokens served from KV cache. The spreadsheet has scenario tabs for 3 models and caching assumptions.
- We usually target a target $/1M tokens metric when comparing offerings; please tell us your target $/1M tokens so we can shape an appropriate commitment and term.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm target $/1M tokens range and procurement timeline? (we discussed March end for PO)
2) If that looks reasonable, I'll push a formal quote (SOW + committed capacity options) — I've attached a draft estimate.
3) Offer to run a short Proof-of-Performance (2-week) on a dedicated pool to validate latency and throughput before go-live.

Attachments: inference_estimate.xlsx (pricing scenarios)

Thanks — I'll follow up with a formal quote once you confirm the target unit economics and preferred option.


Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Kapoor <samir@finlytics.com>

Thanks Dylan — useful recap. A few clarifying questions from our side and some procurement context: 

1) Token counts: the 300M number is current combined (chat + nightly batch). Peak day could push to ~50M tokens/day during product launches. Are the throughput numbers above per-PoP or global pool?
2) Our procurement band for next fiscal year is fairly tight: target operational spend for inference is in the $1.8M - $3.6M range annually (so roughly $150k - $300k/month). We need to understand what committed level gets us into the lower end of the $/1M token range.
3) Procurement timeline: legal + PO targeted by March 31st. We will need a clear SOW and a standard third-party vendor questionnaire answered (I can share it).

Also attaching a small sample of our Feb usage for modeling. Can you confirm whether Option C would meet our peak throughput needs without additional burst capacity?

Thanks — looping in procurement (procurement@finlytics.com) on the cc.

Attachment: finlytics_usage_feb.csv


Samir Kapoor
Head of ML Platform, FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing - FinLytics follow-up

Hi Samir — appreciate the context and timeline. Answers and a more explicit unit-econ breakdown below.

Quick answers
- Throughput numbers I quoted are for a single dedicated pool serving your workload globally (we can split regionally if you prefer). Option C (16x A100) should comfortably cover 50M tokens/day peaks with headroom for bursts; we can add temporary burst capacity if you expect irregular spikes.
- If target monthly spend is $150k/month (~$1.8M/year), Option B (4x H100) is below that; Option C (~$120k-$165k/month) is closer to the midpoint depending on term and discounting.

Unit economics worked example (Option C, conservative):
- Estimated committed price: $140,000 / month (midpoint for 16x A100)
- Forecast token volume (steady state): 1.2B tokens / month
- Cost per 1M tokens = (140,000 / 1,200) = $116.67 per 1M tokens (note: this is illustrative — model choice and caching change the effective cost).

For transparency, here are three modeled scenarios (spreadsheet tab names match):
- Low scale (300M tokens/mo): at $120k/month committed -> ~$400 / 1M tokens
- Mid scale (600M tokens/mo): at $130k/month committed -> ~$217 / 1M tokens
- High scale (1.2B tokens/mo): at $140k/month committed -> ~$117 / 1M tokens

Why the big delta? Dedicated pricing is mostly a fixed GPU commit. As token volume scales, the $/1M token falls materially. That's why scaling with a larger reserved pool (Option C) drives the best unit economics.

Proposal & next steps
1) If your procurement target is $150k/month, we should evaluate Option C with a 12/24-month term to hit the lower $/1M numbers.
2) I'll circulate a formal quote + SOW draft (will include SOC2 evidence link and the questionnaire response).
3) We recommend a 2-week PoP on a trimmed dedicated pool before full provisioning; we can price that as a discounted evaluation (credit against first month).

I'll attach a draft SOW and an example commitment table for your procurement team. Let me know which option you want a formal quote on and I'll get contracts started.

Attachments: finlytics_sow_draft.pdf, inference_estimate.xlsx


Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
